We have two subnetworks. The measurements indicate overall network total resistance between A and B is 66.364, which matches sum of all resistors (calculated series total). The current topology we tried (simply connecting subnet1 between A-B and subnet2 branching from B to X1) gave huge errors. We need to combine subnetworks correctly to match measurements.

We need to infer how they connect. Subnet1: A-B-R1 (2.727), B-C-R2 (5.455), C-X1-R3 (8.182). So path A-B-C-X1.

Subnet2: B-N_b3-R1 (20), N_b3-N_b2-R2 (15), N_b2-N_b1-R3 (10), N_b1-X1-R4 (5). So path B -> N_b3 -> N_b2 -> N_b1 -> X1.

Thus overall network likely has two parallel paths between B and X1? Actually both subnetworks share nodes A, B, X1, and also maybe C is internal. Subnet1 goes A-B-C-X1. Subnet2 goes B-...-X1. So overall network: A connected to B via R1_1 (2.727). Then from B to X1 there are two parallel branches: one via C (R2_1+R3_1 = 5.455+8.182=13.637) and another via N_b3,N_b2,N_b1 (20+15+10+5=50). Also there is a direct path? No direct resistor between B and X1 besides those branches.

Thus overall network: A-B series resistor (2.727). Then from B to X1 parallel combination of 13.637 and 50. Then X1 maybe connects to something else? Measurements also include A to X1 resistance 16.364. Let's compute: series R_AB + parallel of 13.637 and 50. Parallel: 1/(1/13.637+1/50)=? Compute.
